newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Papua stocks bounce back as crisis fears ease.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Papua stocks bounce back as crisis fears ease.

text.p: Shares in Papua New Guinea (PNG) resource companies including Oil Search Ltd and Lihir Gold bounced back on Tuesday after investor fears on the PNG crisis eased.

PNG prime minister Sir Julius Chan late on Monday sacked the commander of the PNG defence force after he demanded that Chan resign over the decision to hire mercenaries to solve the deadlock on Bougainville Island.
At 11.05 p.m. (0005 GMT), Oil Search shares were seven cents up at A$2.67, Lihir Gold was four cents up at A$2.14 and Niugini Mining Ltd was one cent up at A$2.97.

"They have come back a little bit, it shows yesterday was a bit overdone," said Scott Healy, a dealer at Brisbane-based brokers Wilson HTM. "But the next 48 hours is going to be crucial to investor sentiment," Healy said.
Healy said the general feeling is that stocks were oversold, that the companies had nothing to do with the central issue -- the conflict on Bougainville island.

At 11.20 p.m. (0020 GMT), Orogen Minerals Ltd, which is 51 percent owned by the PNG government, was steady at A$3.20 after hitting a low of A$2.98 earlier. Orogen closed 24 cents down at A$3.20 on Monday.
Shares in Bougainville Copper Ltd, owner of the disputed copper mine on Bougainville, were also steady at 55 cents. Its shares fell five cents on Monday.
Bougainville's Panguna copper mine was shut down in 1989 at the start of rebellion when landowners were refused a greater interest in the running of the mine.
